newsitem.title: USA: TELE-TV downsizing came as no surprise to analysts.
newsitem.headline: TELE-TV downsizing came as no surprise to analysts.

text.p: The decision to scale back the TELE-TV partnership, formed by three telecommunications companies in 1994, came as no surprise to analysts, who said the venture had been foundering for the past year.

Bell Atlantic Corp, NYNEX Corp and Pacific Telesis Group on Friday said they planned to scale back the interactive television venture and eliminate 100 TELE-TV jobs, or about half of its total workforce, in several cities across the United States.
"Everyone's been anticipating that in some fashion TELE-TV would wind down," Credit Suisse First Boston analyst Frank Governali said.
Analysts said the move seemed inevitable and had been expected because the interactive television market has failed to take off as initially expected.

Gary Arlen, president of Arlen Communications of Bethesda, Maryland, which watches the industry, said a key obstacle to interactive TV and video-on-demand has been resistance among its target audience -- consumers 40 years old and older, who would rather be true couch potatoes when watching television.
The industry may eventually take off as younger consumers come of age, he said. In the interim, TELE-TV has struggled, he said.
"TELE-TV is a company that has been searching for a mission for the past six months," Arlen said.

The venture was formed in 1994 by the three companies as an efficient way to support their individual video strategies. It was set up to develop home entertainment, information and interactive services.

However, the partners said in a joint statement their "evolving strategies for video services made it clear that it was simply not cost effective to support the current level of TELE-TV operations for the forseeable future."
Since the venture began, Bell Atlantic has agreed to merge with NYNEX, and Pacific Telesis has become a subsidiary of SBC Communications Inc.

TELE-TV Chairman and Chief Executive Howard Stringer said Friday he had resigned from the company. The announcement came the same day as published reports of speculation that Stringer was in talks to take a senior position at Sony Corp of America.
((-- Lisa Marie Pane, New York newsdesk, 212 859-1713))
